Enough! You have proven my kin and I are no match for your brutality.

You seek to return us to our meek lives and violent deaths? So be it. Even so, this is MY domain, and though you have shown you have no trouble harming my kin you are not welcome to openly prey on them. You would do best to leave this place, mortal.

Go then, scurry back to your dark-feathered master. Tell her we will relent... for now.

This is terrible. Why would a druid do this to a Wild God? 

As for this "Pact"... I've heard whispers of a group of apostate druids that broke away from the Circle. The Blackthorne Pact, they call themselves... but I'd never have dreamed that they would be capable of something like this.

This is terrible. Just terrible.

progress.text: The trees with shade around their lower bark hide the most Moonveil moss.
Harpy magic is raw and primal, able to be shaped by sages.

complete.text: <Osi immediately pops one into her mouth.> You found some ripe ones! Thanks, I will start to make jam now.

progress.text: On the wide hill, if a dark shape looms on you, duck and hide!

complete.text:
I am relieved to know that the magic we created was effective. It seems that this "oldstone" had at least one more bit of useful magic inside of him. I will also consider Tiala's offer... perhaps. 

We have done good work together, and I hope that you will not forget this lesson: the wilds are bounteous, and beautiful, and they are worth protecting.

I give you one last gift, a memento of our time together.
You bring hope to our tribe. The chance to be friends is clear. Thank you, with your help the trees can stay tall and strong.

accept.text: <Penned in faded ink, the note is requesting $2oa Earthen Silk Belt, along with information about delivery location and payment. At the bottom appears text denoting this writ is transferable.>

objectives.text: Acquire the items requested by the customer and deliver them to the location marked on your map. This writ must be in your possession to complete the transaction.

accept.text:
Some may speak with you now, but not all. For more of our tribe to be what you know as friend, you must not rush.

Stay by our side, work with our young and old, and guard us from those who wish us harm.

When you have more to bring to us, we will have more to share.

objectives.text: Raise your reputation with the Barkskin Burrow to Neutral.

accept.text:
Our warhorses come from two nearby farms. One of them, owned by the Wheeler family off the road just outside of town, has apparently lost all of their stock. The cause of this is currently unknown.

With no horses, we have no cavalry, and without cavalry, our campaign against the Horde stands no chance.

Thus, you see, this situation must be resolved with utmost haste. Of where to start, however, I am less sure.

Go to Wheeler's Grange and speak to Benjy. See what he has to say for himself.

objectives.text: Go to Wheeler's Grange to inquire about the missing horses.

accept.text:
You seen those murlocs down by the river, just west of here? Nasty things. Bad for my animals, and bad for the wildlife. Not to mention, they've settled right on top of my favorite fishing spot!

There ain't a soul in the Riverglades who wouldn't appreciate you getting rid of a few, that's for sure. 

Please, kill any you see. You'd be doin' us a whole heap of good.

objectives.text: Kill 8 Mudfin Oracles and 8 Mudfin Warriors along the river near Wheeler's Grange.

complete.text: How many Scourge you have ta kill on da way here? Never mind, we just don't see too many people out here. Da village been trapped in dis corner of da mountain for a long time.

accept.text:
When you look around you, what do you see? A broken home and a tired people.

Stormwind has left us to fend for ourselves, and we have less to do that with every day. Many within these walls are refugees who barely escaped tragedy without so much as even their own families.

Farholde is no Stormwind, stranger. We lost a settlement in the northwest to the Twilight's Hammer, but we will not let them keep it. If you wish to fight, go to Sunnyglade and purge those savages from our lands.

objectives.text: Defeat $1oa Twilight Raiders, $2oa Twilight Shadowmancers, and $3oa Twilight Neophytes within Sunnyglade for Demar Brant.

accept.text:
You've seen the ruined city to the north, yes? Sunnyglade? Demar tries sending troops, but we're no closer to reclaiming it. I have a better idea.

In truth, this attack by the Twilight's Hammer is not the first. They seem to be coordinating from a centralized location, and I would know where. While you're out doing what you adventurers do best, see if you can't keep an eye out for any documents they may have misplaced. With enough of them, I should be able to piece together their intentions.

objectives.text: Collect $1oa Twilight Pages from within Sunnyglade for Ashe Amberall in Farholde Keep.

accept.text:
My, what have we here? A brave new $c come to save us from our woes? How charming! Maybe you can help me with something then? I'd quite like to learn more about this cult in Sunnyglade.

Like any cult, they operate in a caste system. Those with an affinity for magic are often in high favor and are given tokens to demonstrate such. These charms are then imbued, and thus have a rich abundance of cultist magic.

I wish to see these tokens for myself. Be a dear and see if you can bring me a few, hmm?

objectives.text: Retrieve $1oa Twilight Charms from Twilight Shadowmancers and Twilight Neophytes in Sunnyglade for Ashe Amberhall in Farholde Keep.

complete.text:
So... this Ve'han Talongrasp. The name is known to me. A former druid of the Cenarion Circle. 

But harming a Wild God? Why would he do this? To what end? To kill even a lesser demigod of the wilds is... Well, it's not something that a mortal should even be capable of.
A true hunter, eh? You bringin' da safety to us here.

accept.text:
Our training dummies are starting to show significant wear and tear. If we don't fix them up soon I worry our recruits may be unprepared for battle.

If you hadn't seen it on your way in, there's a small farmstead just outside the keep run by a man by the name of Wheeler. He may have a few extra bushels of hay he'd be willing to part with.

I'll see to it he's compensated if he's able to spare supplies for our efforts.

objectives.text: Collect $1oa Bundles of Hay for Ember at the training grounds.

complete.text:
Yeah, we know about the survivors in the village.

Fandral gave us specific instructions not to interact with them.

No, I don't know why. Fandral says a lot of things that I don't agree with. Not that I always follow rules... sometimes I've dropped off a little food just outside the village when nobody's looking.

But he won't let us help them off the mountain. Doesn't want them "interfering" with things up here. I guess he has other plans.

Ha! I could see the explosions from here. That will set those meddling mortals back for at least a while.

Well done, dirtwalker, well done!

<The crow lets out a series of strange caws you realize is laughter.>

Don't fret, the land will eventually heal. You have done much to start the process, and for that both myself and the mountain thank you.

Venture Co? And the trunk was empty?

Those rotten cheats stole my money! I knew dealin' with those good-for-nothin' pirates was bad for business! Nobody goes back on a deal with Ruzzgot and gets away with it.

accept.text:
I already spent good coin on that crate. We ain't just going to let them have it!

You want your shipment? Go to the Venture Co's camp up north and find out who's responsible for this backstabbin'! This ain't about money anymore, $n. This is about justice! And maybe a little about the money.

objectives.text: Find the Venture Co. Ledger in the Venture Co. Camp near Lake Nezferiti in Stranglethorn.

accept.text:
My husband and I have a farm north of here. I come to Farholde after each harvest to sell what we grow. In good seasons, I like to set aside whatever we don't sell to give to folks who need a little pick-me-up. Gotta take care of your neighbors, I say.

There's a logging camp north of our farm, right on the river. I'm sure those boys could use some fruits and vegetables to give 'em some variety in their diet.

If you're heading that way, could you give this to the foreman there? Name's Halligan Turner.

objectives.text: Deliver Cassandra's surplus farm goods to Halligan Turner at Turner's Logging Camp.

accept.text:
Since brother Lowley and I began serving Farholde in a more secular capacity, the church here has fallen into disuse. I'd like to think that once the fighting is over, we will be able to bring the Light back to this place. Although, I fear that may not be for a long while...

Still, we need to keep the church in working order, in the hope that day will come.

To that end, a colony of bats has taken to roosting in the upper stories of the church. It would be a great help if you could remove them.

complete.text: You are a good soul, $c. Thank you.

objectives.text: Kill 5 Roosting Duskbats in the Farholde Cathedral for Sister Rowland.

accept.text:
While we no longer hold service at the church, I feel it important to keep the candles lit on the graves of our fallen in the church's crypt. To me, keeping the candle's flame alive is a symbol that they are not forgotten and their sacrifices were not in vain.

If you would, bring me candles so that I might continue this ritual. It would mean a great deal to me.

If you're not sure where to find them, speak with Marla in the house just outside of the church. She's a friend and may have some to spare.

complete.text: These will do marvellously. I thank you again for your help, $N.

objectives.text: Bring $1oa Holy Candles to Sister Rowland in Farholde Keep.

progress.text: I know a few candles are a small gesture in the grand scheme of what we're doing here, but just as I care for the living, so too must I care for the dead.

accept.text:
If you don't mind, I'd like you to do the honor of lighting these memorial candles. Go to the cemetery just outside and place a fresh candle wherever you see one that's gone out.

Such a task is a far cry from the excitement of your other adventures, I'm sure. Think of this as an opportunity for service and reflection--a quiet moment to acknowledge those who left this world before us, so that we might carry on and make it a better place.

complete.text:
The souls of our fallen look upon you with warmth and gratitude, as do I.

Thank you for helping keep the church alive, $N. May the Light guide and protect you on your journey.

objectives.text: Place $1oa Memorial Candles on graves in the chapel graveyard for Sister Rowland at Farholde Keep.

progress.text: All out of candles, $N?

accept.text:
Hey pal, you look like you can handle yourself in a fight.

Baron Revilgaz has me keep'n my ear to the ground for magical objects. Word on the street is that a sunken troll ruin has mysteriously become, eh, un-sunk, which means there are a lot of unclaimed goods, if you catch my meaning.

Problem is, it's also caught the eye of pirates! Not just any pirates, the Saltseers specifically collect magical artifacts. I need you to go into the Drowned City, clear them out and take their stolen artifacts.

objectives.text: Collect $1oa Voodoo Infused Artifacts from Saltseer pirates in the Drowned City.

accept.text:
The Saltseer pirates have been a thorn in my side recently and knowing they're in the Drowned City makes it worse! I mean they're always bad news, but there is one captain in particular I want outta the picture. That damned Captain Dreadrise!

He and his crew are very accomplished at gathering all the magical artifacts I've been after, and I'm tired of the competition.

I want you to remove Captain Dreadrise and his Saltseer Coroners from the picture. Permanently.

objectives.text: Slay 3 Saltseer Coroners and Captain Dreadrise in the Drowned City.

accept.text:
You there! I have a job for someone of your... skills.

I have gotten word from my sources of a crystal found in Shaper's Terrace that can seemingly drain the elements around it. Or perhaps it can drain life essence itself. It is unclear from this report.

I must have a fragment of this crystal! Just think of the applications of such a powerful artifact.

Go to Shaper's Terrace and bring me back a sample of this colorless Achromatic Crystal, and I will reward you for your efforts.

objectives.text: Gather a colorless Drained Crystal Fragment near the Achromatic Crystal in the Shaper's Terrace.

accept.text:
G'day, $Glad:lass;. Name's Bertrand, Bertrand Ironbrow! At yer service.

<Bertrand extends a filthy hand.>

These fine folk contracted me tae oversee construction of this here keep. What they lack in experience they make up for in spirit! Problem is, I misplaced me tools.

Had a bit of a run in with a few Twilight in a small grove northwest o' here. Had to choose between me life or me tools. On one hand, I'm alive. On the other... ye see where this is goin'.

Think ye could help find me tools?

objectives.text: Locate the Foreman's Crate and return it to Bertrand Ironbrow in Farholde Keep.

progress.text: You get the grub? The wolves are startin' to look hungry...

complete.text: Astonishing. I'll share our findings with the others. Perhaps now is our time to reclaim the area once and for all.

accept.text:
Although I am sure we can attribute the damage to both pylons to the reckless centaur stomping about, I suspect the timing of their rampage resulted in the shards being separated. I know little about their quarrels, but I do know there are at least two main factions that have trespassed into Shen'dralas: the ferocious Magram and the cunning Gelkis.

Keeping these treasures in the midst of a battlefield would be unwise. By now, I am assuming they have taken their trophies back to their own villages.

complete.text:
The crystals are in a few more pieces than I was expecting, but this looks to be all of it. I will hold onto these for the moment. Thank you, $N.

Your next step will be to gather mana that is malleable enough to serve as both an adhesive for the broken pieces, and a conduit for the leylines to surge through thereafter.

It is quite a remarkable process, but gathering the mana may prove to be an inconvenience.

objectives.text: Recover shards and fragments of the pylons, found guarded at the Magram and Gelkis villages. Return them to Mordent Evenshade.

progress.text: I would rather not further draw the centaur's attention toward me or my fallen kin, else I would seek out the crystals myself.

accept.text:
You may have seen the floating sparks of mana scattered throughout Shen'dralas. This is a new phenomenon, likely the result of the damage the pylons have endured.

We need this mana back in a semicrystallized form. We can accomplish this by using the Mana Sieve found within the temple. Borrow the sieve and collect any floating mana orbs you find.

The temple's denizens will not appreciate their precious artifact being borrowed without their consent, but they will understand in time.

complete.text:
I see you have successfully repaired the pylons--how could I not notice?

<Mordent gestures up and toward the skies, his gaze briefly followed in that direction as well. As his attention returns to you, he lofts his brow as he takes note of your seemingly lesser levels of enthusiasm.>

objectives.text: Acquire the Mana Sieve from within the temple in Shen'dralas and use it to collect Ancient Mana Crystals. Once you have acquired enough mana, empower the pylons and return to Mordent Evenshade.

progress.text: It is good to see you again, $N.

complete.text: You've certainly earned quite the reputation here. Pleasure to finally meet you.

<Master Gadrin listens closely as you explain your journey and how you came to possess the I'lalai tablet etchings.>

It was good of Kin'Weelay to send you here. I am grateful you both have taken such a strong interest in preserving and discovering parts of our ancestral heritage we have lost over the centuries. I am also pleased to see mention of a new loa. I will begin looking into this mystery myself.

Anyway, Kin'weelay asked me to give this to you, as thanks for all your efforts for our tribe.

<Ketharas gently takes the staff and feather from you. He holds the feather in his palm for a moment and closes his eyes, then frowns deeply.>

Come, $c, you must tell me all about this staff you have found.

This magic... I feel that this could be the beginning of a very important turning point for us here on the mountain. For good, perhaps? More likely, I fear, it is for ill.

You have found the Shrine of Aviana, traveler, and we two--myself and Skylord Omnuron--are its last guardians.

The Wormwings would exterminate us if they could, but we defend this place with the grace of the sky goddess. Her dream lives on through us.
What is this, little mortal? A branch? How curious...

Though they may look like simple bangles to the outsider, each piece is a treasured part of our history, and an important part of a harpy's coming of age. Only those that have become adults may don ornamentations.

The blood smeared across them pains me, but it will help me remember the travesty that has occurred here. Hopefully when these are passed to the next generation, the weight of the lives lost will not be as heavy as it is today.

Thank you, $c.

progress.text: I mourn that my sisters' blood had not even cooled before these prized possessions were ripped from their bodies.

complete.text:
Whoa, what happened to you? You look terrible. I mean, you did anyway, but you look extra terrible and caked with goo.

<Felflick listens as you recount the slime encounter and grins.>

Really now? Fascinating. I guess the slime eating the first 'Master of Slimes' warlock did something, and the newly added warlock bones gave it a bit of awareness? I wonder if their minds all fused together at the end.

Well regardless, I'll keep that little gem in the back of my mind for later.

<Phoebe cringes as you show her the corrupted knots from the nearby trees.>

This is far worse than I was hoping. With the Wormwings taking over, the infection has spread much faster than previously. My sisters and matrons were originally the ones overseeing the removal of it.

Removing these corrupted knots will not completely fix the problem, but is akin to lancing an infected wound. It will help, even if only a little.

Thank you for taking the time to care for my home, $c.

progress.text: The potency of the Well of Eternity, and its various effects, seem to always be shifting.
The spirits of our kaldorei ancestors will never truly disappear from these lands, but we can assist them on their journey.

complete.text:
<The crow looks bemused as you recount your time with Felflick and what you've learned.>

Oh, no. The key didn't work? Shame. I guess any old key you find in the dirt might not be the correct one, hum? But what would a little crow like me know of such things?

And you're sure they said the word 'Blackthorne'? Interesting.

Anyhow, two demons with one stone as they say. It would seem we've at least stemmed the threat for the time being.

Well done, dirtwalker. I hereby pronounce you as my underwing!
<There is something deeply unsettling about this bone pile. Perhaps caution would be wise?>

It's... it's too much, yet. The darkness in my mind clouds how I remember it.

Could he be in the same torpor, restless as I was? Soul suffocated by the stench of walking amongst the dead?

Ah, thank you, $c. This is direly needed. Though it will not purge the infection, it will help ease the suffering as the infection takes its course.

Unfortunately there is little else I can do for my fellows at this point but offer them wisdom and soothe their pain.

progress.text:
Have you brought the herbs? My eyesight isn't what it used to be after the war, and after my injury I am not as stable on my feet as I once was as a young orc.

<Ortak smiles sadly.>

Such is the price of war and time. Though it seems you may know of these sorrows yourself. It seems life has not been kind to you. I hope you have found more peace in your... new life.

accept.text:
I would ask one last favor while I have you here, friend. Could you deliver the poultice I have made to two of my companions here in camp?

Enho is in our infirmary to the left. He is very weak but I yet hope he will be able to overcome the infection. I have been spoon-feeding him broth to try to help him regain his strength.

The other is Maruke.

<Ortak hangs his head in silence for a moment.>

You will find her north of here, where we keep the few mounts we have left.

objectives.text: Deliver the Hyjal Silphium Poultice to Enho and Maruke.

progress.text: Bad voodoo is bad for ya. Remember that, mon.

accept.text:
I have had a vision.

Deep in the place known as Maraudon, past the earth song falls, there is a chamber filled with brilliant white crystals and guarded by mighty giants. At the highest part of this chamber is a crystal of exceptional brilliance. It is an aspect of the sun god, the right eye of the Earthmother herself--An'she.

I've dreamed of its radiance and it calls to me. $c, remove An'she's Radiance from that place and bring it here where it belongs, under the open skies of Mulgore.

objectives.text: Recover the crystal known as An'she's Radiance from Maraudon.

accept.text:
You there, $c. I have a matter I could use assistance with.

I just so happen to be writing a thesis on the ancient Wildhammer runemasters of Grim Batol, and there's a particular tome I need to complete my research. According to our ledgers, a mage by the name of Doan checked the book out of the old Dalaran library before the Third War and never returned it!

Arcanist Doan is now holed up in the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades. Retrieve this book for me and you'll be well rewarded.

objectives.text: Retrieve the book The Lost Magic of the Runemasters from the Scarlet Monastery.

accept.text:
We see fewer and fewer travelers from Razor Hill these days. The scorpids were never much fun, but now I hear there are spiders making their nest along the road.

If your travels take you up north, kill some of the spiders on your way. Then, let Razor Hill know the path's a bit safer for them.

complete.text: The peons have been scared to travel south for some time, $N. Now that you've cleared the path a bit, we can get them back to work.

objectives.text: Kill 6 Ridgeshade Creepers and 6 Ridgeshade Lurkers in southern Durotar, then report to Gar'thok in Razor Hill.

progress.text: Have you done what I asked?
Did you find the fruits?

complete.text:
If the sight of you wasn't enough, your words confirm it, then. Travelers have returned to Hyjal!

This warrior you met imparting mountain mercy is right--I have shared visions and sights during ancestral calling and channeling.

These flying terrors have become poisoned, worse to encounter than the demonic wings they replaced. We will stay on guard from the skies.

progress.text: Something need doing?

complete.text:
Greetings again, Dirtwalker! You are still alive, it seems. It would also seem you've talked to that oldstone-in-the-cave, Ketharas.

So, what have you learned since last we spoke, hmm?

<The crow listens intently as you explain the journey Ketharas has sent you on thus far.>

A mortal... did this? Yes, yes, yes. You will need the aid of the other gods of Hyjal, indeed. Luckily for you, I think I may know just the benevolent bird to get your flight started!

Ah, dirtwa-, I mean mortal! What has brought you to my domain?

<Jereman listens to you as you recount your adventure on Hyjal with what appears to be a bemused expression.>

I see you have met the brightest and most clever bird of my flock. She is, of course, beloved by all. Only second to myself, naturally.

She was right to send you to me. So, that oldstone needs to draw upon the power of the Wild Gods, does he? Very well, then.

What have we here? An $r that speaks? Well this is... new. I'm not used to my food speaking to me by choice. Curious. I do wonder what could have possibly possessed you to come to me. You realize I eat corpses.

<Marrosis stares down his beak at you with a dour, and almost tired expression.>

Oh. You were sent here by HER weren't you? I do hope she didn't accompany you.

<He looks to the sky with the closest expression to a scowl a bird can make.>

The last thing I need is for that old crow to stick her talons in my business again.

progress.text:
Have you collected the bones I asked for? I am sure it seems like an odd request.

Admittedly it is much slower for one such as myself to collect them. There are only so many bones I can delicately grasp in my talons before I accidentally crush them to powder.

<Marrosis sighs, looking annoyed.>

Before you ask; no, I have no intention of building some kind of shrine. That was HER suggestion. That is the last time I ask for any ideas from her or her flock.

complete.text:
The demon commanders will be drawn out by the smell of these bonfires being lit anew.

This is our chance to end their reign.

Well, well, well. How unexpected! A mortal here on Hyjal that is willing to risk life and limb to come and visit me in my abode. What brings you to my lands, hmm?

<Renalard's mischievous expression grows and he bares his teeth in what appears to be a wide grin.>

Ah, so it was Jereman who sent you! Well, why didn't you say so sooner? My, it has been some time since she came flapping about here last. Naturally I do have the answers to this little puzzle she has sent my way.

Ha HA! I watched you from here. Ah, to hoodwink a demon. It's not difficult, but it's always entertaining!

Now that I have a whole pile of these supplies... well, you don't need to worry about that. I guarantee they'll be put to good use. You can thank me later!

progress.text:
Oh, you're back already? Did you have a chance to use that fox fur I gave you? I promise the results will be amusing.

<Renalard grins at you with a mouth filled with too many teeth.>

complete.text:
Stay back, wielder of fire and metal! Perhaps you are accustomed to my kind being your prey, but no more!

Jereman is not the only god on this mountain. Take care, mortal, lest you cross a power greater than your own. You meddle in the affairs of gods at your own peril!

The way ahead is clear if I stay on the road? Harpies are exactly the kind of enemy I'm trying to avoid. 

Thank you, and for refilling the gourd. I hope you took the time to refresh yourself at the falls while you were there.

When I perform my rituals of blessing, I will use this water to honor the mountain's past and its caretaking spirits.

progress.text: I need to spend more time in the hills. This thin air demands much from the body.

complete.text:
The fall of one of their commanders has weakened the Legion's nerve. The chaos will allow my blade to cleave their divisions wide apart.

You have fought beside me at a decisive moment, and your resolve has not wavered. For that, you have my regard. May the mountain's spirits judge you worthy of what you carry forward.

Part of our rite is to pass on weaponry. This is yours now. Value what life in it still remains.

Our paths may cross again, but they do not run together. Farewell.

accept.text:
Ey mon! Today be a big day for ya, I see. Ya think you're ready to take de reins of one of these fierce creatures, huh?

Most be underestimatin' how intelligent and savage these beasts be. Ya won't be findin' a better, faster or more lethal companion once ya be bonded with it.

So, you be havin' an important choice to make. Ya raptor and you will be traversin' the world together, and the raptor will also be needin' to choose ya in return.

Go an' take a look and return to me when ya made ya choice.

complete.text:
Ah, good. I be seein' in your eyes that you have made a choice. A fine one at that.

De one you have picked seems fond of you already, though I am not surprised. I hope you two be taking good care of each other out there in de world.

Blessings of Gonk go wit ya both.

objectives.text: Inspect the riding raptors to choose your first mount.

complete.text:
Galvinquam's bags will join the other gear we're restoring. I see he carried more than he thought--there are tools tucked in here that will serve us as we rebuild.

You've eased his journey and given us time to prepare a proper welcome for one raised on the low plains. The mountain asks much of those who climb it for the first time.

Thanks to you, his heart will meet the summit with strength left to give.

progress.text: If you're looking for a place to rest, try the remains of the inn just down the road south of here.
Days be gettin' faster...

complete.text:
Dis... dis be his. My big brudda, Qujo. So many seasons gone by, an' da cloth still hold his mark. Da spirits be kind to leave somethin' behind.

My brudda walked da old paths wit' pride. He hunted so others could sleep.

Ya bring him home when ya bring dis back. Dat matter. More den gold, more den words.

Sen'jin gonna honor both ya names 'round the fire tonight.

progress.text: Life by da sea? Shore be nice.

complete.text:
A worthy offering.

Wicked protrusions--horns, spines, armor--shatter into cruel shards. Even in ruin, they hunger to wound.

I will bind these spikes and enhance them with my own runic fire. Let the Legion feel their own strength turned against them. Let them feel the fear that they have struck into the hearts of mortal races.

Their pain is my purpose.

progress.text: Demons are meant to be slain. With their own cruel implements we will hasten their deaths.

complete.text:
Well struck. From above, they broke quickly--just as planned.

You earned this. It will see effective use in your capable hands.

One day I will walk beside others again. When Hyjal is clear of demonic menace once and for all. There is always another front, another corrupter to end.

Be the demons' fear.

accept.text:
If you're headed into Shaper's Terrace, I would ask a favor of you.

There are reports of slimes that live in the pools by the colorless Achromatic Crystal. I believe their essence could be of use in my experiments, and would like you to bring me some samples for study.

I will make it worth your while.

objectives.text: Gather $1oa Seeping Slime Essence in the Shaper's Terrace.

accept.text:
Muln tells me that there is a location in the deepest depths of a place called Blackrock Mountain where the barrier between Azeroth and the elemental plane has been damaged, allowing a myriad of elemental creatures from the realm of the Firelands to escape into this reality, including giants as large as an Anchor Pylon!

I'd very much like to study any fragments of material that could be gathered from one of these creatures. Would you brave the Blackrock Depths and recover a sample for me?

objectives.text: Recover a Fragment of the Firelands from Blackrock Depths for Alaana Stormwalker in Mulgore.

accept.text:
Ey, welcome $c! Ya now be seasoned enough as an adventurer for me to teach you how to ride one of our raptors, for a fee of course.

Zjolnir will provide ya with a free mount once you have trained with me, and after you will be able to purchase any additional mounts ya would like. There are many creatures out in the world, and each requires their own riding skill, but ya will have to find trainers for each.

Speak to me when ya have enough gold, and I will teach ya about raptor riding.

complete.text:
Spirits be with ya, $c. I'm happy to see you've completed your training with Xar'Ti.

She is masterful at handling these raptors and helping one learn the bond between raptor and rider. Riding one of these beautiful creatures ain't be for the faint of heart.

objectives.text: Learn the Apprentice Riding skill from Xar'ti.

progress.text:
The Bloodtalon are known for their cunning and swiftness, and make fine companions when raised from egg to adult.

Unfortunately adult raptors are very difficult to train, and I have tried to capture the Matriarch on more than one occasion. But she had become too dangerous of late.

Still I hope to preserve her legacy by raising her children as companions here in Sen'Jin.

accept.text:
When we fled the isles that Zalazane and his ilk now inhabit, we left behind many precious idols that help us commune with spirits we worship: our loa. They are of grave importance to our tribe.

The followers of Zalazane show no reverence for our loa and have scattered these idols across the largest of the isles.

This is an action that will not go unnoticed if we are not able to collect these idols, and offending a loa is a grave matter.

Go, find as many loa idols as you can and return them to me.

objectives.text: Collect 8 Forgotten Loa Idols from the Echo Isles. Bring them to Master Gadrin in Sen'jin Village.

progress.text: Have you found our loa idols, $N? We must begin our rituals again soon.

accept.text:
Yelmak doesn't want his apprentice breaking anything. Well, anything more than he already has.

He told me the young mixer in training has too much pride to ask for help when he really needs it. Yelmak wants to give him a taste of a particular home-brewed recipe.

Gather a mix of cattail and speargrass cuttings taken from the plants growing around the water in the Valley of Honor. I'd get them myself, but if I left the shop, Whuut would surely know we're catering to his mood.

objectives.text: Take some cuttings from the Cattails and Speargrass growing around the water flows in the Valley of Honor and return to Kor'geld in Yelmak's Alchemy and Potions.

accept.text:
$n, you have proven you are a strong and dutiful hunter and I am impressed by your bravery. It is only because of this I offer you this hunt.

A wind serpent hunts along a road off the coast of Feralas and has been ambushing travelers, and leaving their corpses strewn about the road. It is clear she does not hunt out of necessity. This is a creature that no longer shares the Earthmother's blessing.

The windserpent Mirrorscale makes her lair at the bottom of the waterfall along the coast of Feralas.

objectives.text: Bring Mirrorscale's Wing to Melor Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff.

complete.text:
Hey, yea, that looks like what had them all rattled. Doesn't look much worse for the wear. Maybe those stiffs will stop breathin' down my neck about lost profits now.

Here, have a little somethin' for the trouble.

progress.text: I can understand why some flashy metal might work to distract one of those oafs, everything they craft is mediogre.

accept.text:
I noticed a few rocks that seemed unusual in the Dustbowl. Upon closer inspection, I saw that they had carvings! I could not resist making rubbings of them to study later.

The nearby ogres took notice of my presence and before I could even react, I woke up under the care of the innkeeper, and with a terrible headache.

Now, I am down all of my supplies and without any study material while I heal. Can you venture to the east in search of my pack, and take rubbings of the etchings yourself?

objectives.text: Slay ogres in the Dustbowl for Mus'hale's Stolen Supplies and use them to collect rubbings of the nearby stone etchings, then return to Mus'hale at Kargath.

accept.text:
Any experienced shaman who attempts to scry the elemental plane can tell you that there is a blip of sorts, a distortion that you feel as you cross over to the other realms of existence.

We have need of adventurers like yourself to help us better understand this disturbance. Take this Elemental Attractor. You will be able to extract motes of unstable magic with it from the most skilled spellcasters and other powerful entities you may encounter. Bring me these motes so that we may study them.

objectives.text: Bring $1oa Motes of Unstable Magic to Nuara Tremorhoof.

accept.text: The battle at the Darkspear Islands be locked in a stalemate, $c. Show those Alliance fools who the superior force is. Carry your head high in service of the Darkspear and claim victory in battle. The Loa will surely be givin' you their blessing, $c!

objectives.text: Win a Darkspear Islands battleground and return back to Nizook Boof at The Merchant Coast.

complete.text:
Heglan's body lies cold within the wreckage of the hut.

Whatever killed her doesn't seem to be human. There may be signs of what happened nearby.

This banner and blade piece belong to the naga! They must have come down the coast from the north.

We cannot let them establish a foothold here. The pressure from both directions would be too much for Razor Hill.

progress.text: Did you find her?

accept.text:
It wouldn't be the first time those snakes bothered us. They need to be taught that their presence is not tolerated here.

Find where their scouts are setting up camp and slaughter them. Bring me back their fins as proof. We need to act fast to make sure they understand.

objectives.text: Collect $1oa Naga Spinefins.

accept.text:
I decided to do a bit of scouting in the crag on my own. Unfortunately my magic ran out at the wrong time and I've been stuck hiding here since.

If you could help me escape, I would appreciate it.

complete.text:
Ah, Pal'juh got herself in trouble again, did she?

Hopefully she learns her lesson about going alone this time. Thank you for helping her. She's a promising hunter, just tends to act more like a raptor than a tiger.

objectives.text: Help Pal'juh escape Kolkar Crag and bring news of your success to Master Vornal in Sen'jin Village.

accept.text:
While I watched in horror as you frolicked through the haunted woods with my precious relic, your meddling did inspire an idea.

The unstable rifts you encountered are the precursors to our pylon guards. We have been unable to conjure more for centuries, and I worry what might happen when those that remain inevitably flicker out.

I know it seems counterintuitive, but see if you can find another pylon protector nearly on the verge of collapse and recover their Crystal Heart. I'll explain more after.

complete.text:
You were successful, I see! And what a heart you recovered. I am excited to know that the passing of centuries did little to tarnish the craftsmanship of this gemstone.

Most importantly, this is a promising discovery. It would seem that, indeed, mana is temporary, but gemstones are forever.

Are you eager to learn what comes next?

objectives.text: Slay a Decrepit Pylon Protector for their Depleted Crystal Heart and bring it to Historian Biraxas within the temple of Shen'dralas.

progress.text: I assure you I am not looking to sabotage one of our only means of defense. If a protector does not look as lively and well-nourished as those in our temple, then they are on the last hundred years or so of their lifecycle. If anything, it is a mercy killing.

accept.text:
While sourcing the gems necessary to conjure the elementals is a challenge itself, the bigger concern is whether there is still enough loose mana in Shen'dralas to create them. With this heart, we can confirm once and for all whether we need to begin researching other means of defense.

For you, the task is simple. Simply toss this gem into one of those unstable rifts. If we're lucky, you'll have a fight on your hands. Don't feel compelled to hold back, if it works once, it will work again.

objectives.text: Throw the Depleted Crystal Heart into an Unstable Mana Rift. Return to Historian Biraxas within the temple of Shen'dralas with proof of success or failure.
